cells.tense: You keep going, and you're still here while it happens.
cells.verb: Going the distance on the strength of what you're still hoping for.
cells.place: In the middle of what you're bringing along, tending it the way it actually needs — conditions rather than shoves.
cells.ask: You're free to feed what this steadiness is already growing. Offer it one place to hold firm — a small pressure you can take the weight of and stay standing under. What comes back is the ease of a hand that holds because it isn't forcing.
cells.core: You keep going on hope that has been tested and hasn't quit. What you hope for has been through weather and you're still here, still tending it, still watching what it's becoming. The showing for it is steady and unforced — not gripping, not pushing, just staying.
cells.sheetLine: You keep showing up for what's still growing, and you don't force it.

cells.tense: You're already bracing for a day that hasn't come.
cells.verb: Persisting past the point where persisting is still faith.
cells.place: Leaning over what's growing, trying to hurry it into bloom before it's ready.
cells.ask: Put something down for one day and let it develop without your hand on it. What comes back is a shine that's earned rather than declared — light because the thing actually finished growing, not because you held it open.
cells.core: You're carrying the end of the road before the road has gotten there. You push the growing thing to be finished, and the push keeps you at the very finish line you're trying to force. The hoping that used to hold you up has turned into gripping, and what you're gripping is a version of the outcome it hasn't reached yet. Somewhere ahead of you is the moment it's all proven, and you're living there — which is costing you the showing-up that made the proof possible.
cells.sheetLine: You're pushing it to bloom before its time, and losing the bloom.

cells.tense: You stopped at a door you already walked through.
cells.verb: Keeping going on hope that hasn't been given anything to stand on.
cells.place: Beside what's growing but not lending it anything — watching rather than tending.
cells.ask: Take up one small act of tending a thing you're growing — soil, water, structure, plain care — and let it be enough. What comes back is the shine of something that actually developed, and the knowledge that proper tending doesn't exhaust you.
cells.core: The persistence is still in you and it isn't moving toward anything. The tending stopped back there somewhere, and you've been standing next to the thing without giving it conditions. What's missing isn't hope — that's still alive in you — it's the responsible tending that would put the hope into contact with what's actually here. You keep going on empty because you stopped letting care take a form.
cells.sheetLine: You never stopped hoping. You stopped tending.

cells.tense: You're already showing up for what's growing, and you're telling yourself you're not.
cells.verb: Persisting on hope you don't count as yours.
cells.place: In the middle of what you're bringing along, calling it nothing while your hands do the tending.
cells.ask: Call one thing you're already doing 'mine,' out loud, once — no credit, just naming. What comes back is a firmness that doesn't force, because the strength you were calling the situation's is actually a capacity that holds things without crushing them.
cells.core: You're already carrying it — the long hoping, the steady showing-up, the not forcing — and you talk about it as if the thing were managing itself. You call it the work, or what it needs, or just how things go. The persistence is running. The claim on it isn't. The one person who should know they're holding the line is the one telling the story as if no one's holding anything.
cells.sheetLine: You're the one holding it steady. You keep calling it the keeping on that does that by itself.
